A null value is a missing value. 58 - Compute (G6): `A/results/evaluate/comparison_compute.json`, written atomically after the last invocation, is exactly `{invocations, arms, all_invocations, system, versions, allocation}`. 59 - `invocations` has one row per scheduled invocation in run order, each exactly `{round, arm, input, status, wall_s, gpu_busy_s, gpu_busy_known, eval_status, eval_wall_s, eval_gpu_busy_s, attributed_usd}`, from `wrap.json`: `wall_s` is `adapter_wall_s` plus the commands' walls, and `attributed_usd` is `(wall_s + eval_wall_s) / 3600 * C/box.json.price_usd_h`, with a null wall counted as 0 and null when the price is unavailable. Rows of `not_run` invocations have null numbers. 60 - `arms` has one row per arm, each exactly `{arm, invocations, wall_s, gpu_busy_s, gpu_busy_known, eval_wall_s, eval_gpu_busy_s, attributed_usd}`, summed over that arm's replicate invocations whatever their status, with a null counted as 0; `gpu_busy_known` is true only when every summed row's flag is. 61 - `all_invocations` is exactly `{invocations, wall_s, eval_wall_s, attributed_usd}`, summed over every row, warmups and failures included, with a null counted as 0. 62 - `system` and `versions` copy the fetched `system.json` and `versions.json` (null when missing or invalid). 63 - `allocation` is the bill of the whole box allocation, which may include work outside this run, exactly `{type, price_usd_h, started_utc, ended_utc, hours, usd, final}` from `C/box.json`. When that record has `ended_utc` and `hours`, they are copied and `final` is true; otherwise `ended_utc` is null, `hours` is the time from `started_utc` to when the file is written, and `final` is false. `usd` is `hours * price_usd_h`. Unavailable fields are null. At takeaways, after a matching allocation record refreshes `C/box.json` (see Compute metadata), the pipeline rewrites the file atomically with only `allocation` recomputed. The run's own share stays `run_box_usd`. 64 Uploads, links, job files, user setup and fetches are outside every invocation row; they remain in the stage's receipts. 65 - Scoring (U58): after the last invocation, `python3 -I m5/score_comparison.py `. It checks the SHA-256 of `C/comparison.json` against `C/comparison_seal.json` and of each sealed harness file against `C/arms_seal.json`, then scores each comparison, in design order, from the replicate rounds only. 66 - Locations: a relative path names one file. A `{glob}` location names the regular files that Python `glob.glob(glob, root_dir=)` returns, sorted by a key that splits the relative path into runs of digits and non-digits, compares digit runs as integers and breaks ties by the path; their contents, each after `select`, are joined by `"\n"` (by `b"\n"` for `bytes`). A side of an (input, replicate) pair is missing when its invocation's status is not `ok`, when the location is under `eval` and `eval_status` is not `ok`, when the location names no file or an unreadable one, when the content cannot be parsed as the output's `format`, or when the selected content is empty (no bytes for `bytes`, no numbers otherwise). 67 - Output comparisons (`agreement`): for each input and replicate where neither side is missing, the comparator compares the two contents. `exact`: identical bytes. Otherwise both contents are parsed as the output's `format` into number lists; different lengths, or a NaN in one list but not at the same position in the other, disagree; equal infinities agree; finite pairs agree when `abs(a - b) <= abs_tol` (`elementwise_abs`) or `abs(a - b) <= abs_tol + rel_tol * max(abs(a), abs(b))` (`elementwise_abs_plus_rel_max`). A pair agrees when every element agrees. Each compared pair records `max_abs_error` and `max_rel_error` over its finite elements (null when none). 68 - Metric comparisons: an arm's value for (replicate, input) is the metric value above. For `pooled_mean`, a replicate's value is the mean over inputs, null when any input's value is null. Per decision unit (the pooled value, or each input): for `paired_replicate`, the differences are `arm - against` per replicate; for `unpaired`, the differences of every arm value with every against value, or of every arm value with the input's reference value. `ratio_at_least` uses the ratio of means `mean(arm) / mean(against)` for `higher_better` and `mean(against) / mean(arm)` for `lower_better`. 69 - Missing values, per decision unit: `n_missing` counts the arm's missing values and, against an arm, the against arm's (for `pooled_mean` a replicate counts once; for agreement a pair with a missing side counts once). With `"void"`, any missing value makes the unit void with reason `"missing_values"`. With `"fail"`, a missing value of `arm` makes the unit `"not_supported"` with reason `"missing_values"`, and otherwise a missing value of `against` makes it void with reason `"missing_values"`. 70 - Eligibility (`given`): for each listed comparison, its outcome for this unit is that comparison's row for the same input when both comparisons are decided per input, and otherwise that comparison's outcome, where `"per_input"` counts as supported only when every row is. When any of these is not `"supported"`, the unit is void with reason `"not_eligible"`. 71 - Interval: for `all_pairs`, `[lo, hi]` is the minimum and maximum of the differences, and needs at least one difference. For `bootstrap`, the ratio of means is recomputed on `bootstrap_resamples` resamples (`B`) with replacement of the unit's paired replicates, drawn from one `random.Random(bootstrap_seed)` stream in comparison order, and `[lo, hi]` is the `(1 - confidence) / 2` and `(1 + confidence) / 2` empirical quantiles (sorted resamples, index `floor(q * (B - 1))`); it needs at least two replicates. `estimate` is the mean difference (`all_pairs`) or the ratio of means (`bootstrap`) on the full data. Too few values gives outcome `"void"` with reason `"insufficient_replicates"`. 72 - Margin value `m`: 0 for a null margin, `x` for `{"abs": x}`. 73 - Outcome per decision unit, in this order: eligibility; then, for agreement, any compared pair that disagrees makes the unit not supported; then the missing-value rule; then the interval's minimum count; then the criterion. The criterion gives `"supported"`, `"not_supported"` or else `"inconclusive"`: agreement is supported when at least one pair was compared, every compared pair agrees and none is missing (with no compared pair, it is void with reason `"missing_values"`); non-inferiority (`higher_better`) is supported when `lo >= -m`, not supported when `hi < -m`; non-inferiority (`lower_better`) is supported when `hi <= m`, not supported when `lo > m`; superiority (`two_sided`) is supported when `lo > m` or `hi < -m`, not supported when `-m <= lo` and `hi <= m`; ratio with `strict` false is supported when `lo >= threshold`, not supported when `hi < threshold`; ratio with `strict` true is supported when `lo > threshold`, not supported when `hi <= threshold`. 74 - `sign` of a unit is `"higher"` when a superiority is supported with `lo > m`, `"lower"` when it is supported with `hi < -m`, and null otherwise. 75 - A comparison's outcome: for `pooled_mean`, its one unit's outcome; for `per_input_all`, supported when every input is supported, not supported when any input is not supported, void when any input is void and none is not supported, otherwise inconclusive; for `per_input_each`, `"per_input"`, with each input's outcome in its rows. 76 - `C/comparison_scored.json`, atomic, is exactly `{comparison_sha256, comparisons, totals}`. `comparisons` follows the design's order, each exactly `{id, arm, against, criterion, unit, outcome, rows}`; `rows` has one row per decision unit (`input` null for `pooled_mean`), each exactly `{input, n, n_missing, estimate, lo, hi, margin_value, threshold, outcome, sign, reason, pairs}`. `n` counts the differences, ratios or compared pairs; `pairs` is null for metric comparisons and, for agreement, the per-replicate rows `{replicate, agrees, missing, max_abs_error, max_rel_error}` (`agrees` null and `missing` true when a side is missing). Numbers are null when void; `reason` is `"missing_values"`, `"insufficient_replicates"` or `"not_eligible"` for a void unit, `"missing_values"` for a unit made not supported by the `"fail"` rule, and null otherwise. `totals` is exactly `{supported, not_supported, inconclusive, void}`, counting decision units over all comparisons. 77 - Exit 0 after writing; exit 1 for invalid or missing input, a seal mismatch or a failed write, with no output file. A missing or invalid `wrap.json` or fetched file is not invalid input; it is a missing value. Diagnostics contain no input content. A scoring failure fails evaluate with `error_class: parse`. 78 - Evaluate status in comparison mode is PASS once `C/comparison_scored.json` was written, whatever the outcomes. Evaluate facts keep every existing key, null in comparison mode.

## The gaps

### G1: m5 cannot compare named arms (`dut/pipeline/m5/SCHEMAS.md`, "Propose, independent votes, and the one-shot gate")

**What it cannot express.**
- Propose ranks only methods from a fixed menu whose sealed headroom is at least 1.05 (`SCHEMAS.md:213`). When none qualifies, the run stops at propose with `no_feasible_method` (`:215`; `m5/pipeline.js:1037–1038`). Run2 ended exactly this way.
- The m5 model is one baseline against one method. That cannot hold the seed's shape:
  - three named configurations (CPU standard, GPU standard, GPU dense);
  - an ordered gate, where CPU/GPU agreement must pass before dense quality is examined;
  - per-case rank-1 and best-of-50 DockQ reported separately;
  - common budget tiers, where an arm that does not fit is recorded as unavailable, never scored as DockQ 0.
- Evaluate's curve already has unavailable-arm points (`:321`) and deterministic tolerances (`:282`), but only for a single baseline/method pair.
- The route's own finding is bounded: it "does not show that no method could speed up the workload" (`:215`). This is the evidence behind the owner's impression: run2 showed a limitation of the menu, not an answer to the seed.

**Blocks:** the final experiment for P2, P3, P4, P5 and P6.

**Existing workaround: partial.** m5 reproduce-only with a hand-written brief ran named arms descriptively (run6: 60/60 jobs complete). But it has no sealed gate, scorer or verdict, and the step rules restrict it to calibrations.

**Smallest change: large.** An optional named-arm comparison mode. It would take a sealed protocol (arms, ordered gates, budget tiers, per-case metrics, rules for unavailable arms) in place of the menu proposal, and reuse evaluate's existing seal, integrity and scorer machinery.

**Risk.** It widens what a seal can contain. Propose's deterministic gate and skeptic ballots would be bypassed for this mode, so the sealed protocol's author becomes the only judge. That makes G2 (a faithful handoff) and G3 (typed readiness) preconditions, not extras.

### G2: the calibration record drops the card's protocol (`dut/pipeline/src/main.js`, the comment beginning "calibration state per card (2026-10-21)")

**What it cannot express.**
- The record carries `required[]`, `anchor` and only `if_lever, if_not, noise_rule, expected` from `predictions` (`main.js:468–478`). It drops:
  - `decision_rule`, although the PLAN has it (`CONTRACT.md:103`);
  - `arms`, `held_fixed`, the budget tiers and the phase gates other than the one tied to each measured input (`CONTRACT.md:101,108,112`).
- `launch.js` measure therefore compiles scalar ratio bands only (`launch.js:55–57`).
- Run6's quantities had no GUESS or PROXY input at all (the physical card shows `required: []`, s07 §B). The measure route could not even have compiled this calibration.

**Blocks:** calibration on the measure route and the final experiment, for P2–P6.

**Existing workaround: partial.** The science step copied the card's protocol into a calibration brief by hand (s04 and s06 `CALIBRATION_BRIEF.md`). Fidelity then depends on that step, and it is checked only by hash.

**Smallest change: medium.** Carry the whole PLAN (or its hash and path) unchanged in each calibration record, and keep the scientific decision separate from the price-band check.

**Risk.** Larger records. A downstream stage could start reinterpreting a decision rule unless the record is marked immutable.

### G3: readiness cannot record missing scientific evidence (`dut/pipeline/CONTRACT.md`, "2.5 PLAN (producer; also the EXTRACT output)")

**What it cannot express.**
- A PLAN number is a typed cost input (`CONTRACT.md:113–122`). An unresolved tolerance (atol, rtol, eps_xyz, eps_eval) is not a number with a price, so it never enters `required[]`.
- The physical card therefore shows `no_unmeasured_input` while it is scientifically blocked (s07 §B and §D). The seed's requirement of justified tolerances before comparative results has no field.

**Blocks:** the final experiment. Directly for P2. Through the agreement gate also for P3 (C2's acceleration is agreement-gated) and for P5 and P6 (the physical card's main study).

**Existing workaround: partial.** Steps record it in prose (s04 §D, s07 §D), and it stays an owner decision.

**Smallest change: medium.** A typed `required_evidence` list in the PLAN (id, kind such as `tolerance`, the phase that must supply it, how it may be justified), surfaced as a separate calibration state.

**Risk.** It adds a new halting state to the tree. Cards that pass today would read as blocked, and the judges' and critic prompts would need to know the field.

### G4: the measure route has no execution chain (`dut/pipeline/launch.js`, the comment "the stage's args file as measure.sh wrote it …")

**What it cannot express.**
- `stage` reads an args file that m4's `measure.sh` wrote (`launch.js:142,154`). That script is not available.
- So design → gate → build → tests → review → launch → post cannot be chained from a compiled measure folder.

**Blocks:** calibration on this route only. The calibrations so far were for P3 and P4.

**Existing workaround: full**, for the calibrations this seed needed. m5 `--stop-after-reproduce` ran them: run4 PASS and run6 PASS.

**Smallest change: large.** A validated stage-argument chain with a watchdog and ledger ingestion.

**Risk.** It is a new controller with a new failure surface. Its value here is low while the m5 workaround holds.

### G5: no route for authorised local evidence (`dut/pipeline/m5/SCHEMAS.md`, "A/intake/ (written by the intake agent; checked by the pipeline)")

**What it cannot express.**
- Intake is told "Never read experiments/, operator/, or control/" (`m5/pipeline.js:92`). It can read the brief through `add_dirs` (run6), but it cannot follow owner-authorised pointers to earlier records.
- Every brief therefore embeds history by hand: run4's E, run4's printed timings, the pins.

**Blocks:** both calibration and the final experiment. In this seed it touched the P3 and P4 calibrations.

**Existing workaround: partial.** Embedding plus `add_dirs`.

**Smallest change: medium.** An owner-authorised, hashed evidence bundle that intake may read and that later stages carry.

**Risk.** It weakens intake's isolation. Records outside the bundle must stay unreadable, and the bundle's hash must be sealed.

### G6: run cost is not the billed allocation (`dut/pipeline/m5/SCHEMAS.md`, "Compute metadata")

**What it cannot express.**
- `run_box_usd` is the intersection of the run window with the allocation (`SCHEMAS.md:337`). It leaves out box time before the run starts and after takeaways ends.
- The seed asks for billed allocation cost, which is neither number.

**Correction to s07.** s07 called run6's USD 1.367 a stage-wall figure. In fact:
- Run6's stage USD sums to 0.858, from reproduce only (`run6/operator/OPERATOR_TAKEAWAY.md:7–14`).
- The Totals figure, 1.3673 (`:26`), matches the run window: 1,495.58 s × 3.29/3600 = 1.3668. So it is `run_box_usd`, not a stage sum.
- The gap stands, smaller than stated: about USD 1.90 by allocation span (s07 §D) against 1.37 reported.

**Blocks:** the final experiment's cost reporting for P3 and P4.

**Existing workaround: partial.** After `down`, `box.json` holds the allocation's `hours` (`SCHEMAS.md:332`). No invoice is on record.

**Smallest change: small.** Report `box.json` `hours` × price as allocation USD next to `run_box_usd`, and the invoice when available.

**Risk.** Negligible. When one allocation serves several runs, the cost is shared and would be double-counted unless it is labelled per allocation.

## Order I would close them in

1. **G2** (medium). It is a precondition for any sealed protocol to reach execution faithfully, and it is low-risk.
2. **G3** (medium). It gives the tolerance decision a field, so readiness is checkable.
3. **G1** (large). This is the change that makes P2–P6 runnable. It consumes G2's protocol and G3's evidence.
4. **G6** (small). It can go in at any time, before the final experiment's cost report.
5. **G5** (medium). Convenience and identity; the hand-embedding workaround works.
6. **G4** (large). Only if the owner wants the tree's own measure route; m5 covers calibration fully.

## What the owner must decide

1. **Whether to approve the contract change G1, with G2 and G3 as its preconditions.** Without it, the seed can be answered only in part:
   - P1 is established (s01).
   - P3 and P4 have calibration screens, but no verdicts (s07 §B).

   If the owner declines, the alternative is to accept that partial answer.

   Run6's GPU outputs were not byte-identical from run to run (39 distinct hashes over 40 files), which bears on this choice.
3. **Approval for the full physical-card experiment.** It is projected above the USD 20 line: about USD 29.6 in timer terms, USD 49.48 by plan (s07 §D).

Recommendation: approve G2 → G3 → G1 as one contract change (`owner_decision = approve_contract_change`).

# s10 assessment: content check of the operator's G2 contract (U54), 2026-11-03

**Scope.** No test, no network, no box contact, no git, no credentials. I read `s08/` and `s09/` (GAPS.json, REQS.json, PARTS.json, ASSESSMENT.md) and the tree run the earlier steps used: `experiments/blind-02/20261103-0124-tree/out/result.json` (T below), its producer plans under `T/../out/work/seed-20261103/`, `dut/pipeline/src/main.js:465–480`, `dut/pipeline/CONTRACT.md:96–122` and `dut/pipeline/m5/SCHEMAS.md:53`. I judged the U54 section as quoted in the step brief. I did not open the `metis-wt` worktree. I judge G2 only, not G1, G3 or G6. I wrote only into `science/s10/`.

## Verdict: partial (build after three fixes and one added field)

Most of the design is sound. U54 does carry the card's record into the run unchanged and pinned by hash (`A/card.json` with `source_sha256`). It adds `name` and `unit`. It has the harness measure on the card's own phase protocol and keeps the card value out of the measured key, at least by instruction. It brings `measured_value` back into a resolved copy without touching `result.json`, and it never fails a stage because a card value turned out wrong. Those parts meet the fields and direction ("both") that `s09/REQS.json` sets for G2.

The remaining defects are all in what the run *decides* from the measurement, and in what the harness can see. Each can be fixed with one revision before anything is built.

### What the design carries, field by field (s09 REQS G2)
| Field | Carried? | Where |
|---|---|---|
| name, unit | yes | the CONTRACT.md change copies them from the plan's `numbers`. The plans give them, e.g. `eval_runtime_s` "seconds" (`work/…/seed/idea/370cabd5/producer.md:563–569`), `admissible_caps` "caps", `agreement_pass` "boolean" (`…/360caa42/producer.md:504–519`), `localized_faults` "faults", `acceptance_contract_ready` "boolean" (`…/R1/interp/8ce94062/producer.md:306–328`). So `record_lacks_units` does not apply. |
| basis, value, differs_in, measured_by, phase | yes | in the record, which is copied unchanged (`main.js:473–474`). `basis`, `value` and `phase.gate` are also used in the score rows. |
| anchor | yes | the record's `anchor` (`main.js:478`). The intake rule (numeric `published_value`, usual citation rules) is consistent with the m5 anchor rules. For the only admissible record the value is a string (`T:393`), so it is correctly not used. `anchor_rule_unfit` does not apply. |
| measured_value | yes | `card:<id>`, then `card_scored.json` rows, then `resolved` entries. |
| **predictions** | **no, only in part** | the record holds only `if_lever, if_not, noise_rule, expected` (`main.js:478`; `T:398–403`). The plan's `decision_rule` (`CONTRACT.md:103`; present in the plan, `370cabd5/producer.md:23`, which begins "Separate conclusions. Acceleration passes only after agreement and when 95% paired-median CPU/GPU complete-wall ratio…") is dropped before the record exists. U54 copies the record unchanged, so the decision rule never reaches the run or the write-back. |

### The record U54 can actually admit
Card mode accepts only `state: "calibration_required"`. In T exactly one record has that state: `seed:idea:2` (`T:358–404`), with one input. `eval_runtime_s` is GUESS, value 60 s, measured by phase `agreement`, line USD 9.87, 3 h (`T:365–387`). Its gate is `{on: "eval_runtime_s", op: "<=", value: 60}` (`T:375–380`). U54 can serve this record in one run (so `needs_several_runs` does not apply), and the write-back also handles several runs.

The reproduce anchors step runs the published protocol at representative scale and writes `out/anchors_measured.json` (`SCHEMAS.md:53`). A per-case evaluator wall is a measurement that step can produce: run6 recorded per-job walls in reproduce, `s07` §A. So `wrong_stage` does not apply. `protocol_not_runnable` does not apply either: the timing is measurable without the G3 tolerances, and the line fits the USD 20 rule. The physical card (`required: []`, `T:255–259`) and the tolerance calibration for P2 cannot enter card mode. That is G3's gap, which I do not judge here.

## Problems and the smallest fix for each

### 1. `band_rule_unfit`: the band contradicts the card's own gate on the admissible record
For `eval_runtime_s` the band is [20, 180] s, but the card's rule is the one-sided gate ≤ 60 s. Two cases show the contradiction:
- **Measured 100 s:** verdict `within_band`, yet the card's gate fails and its `else` says stop (`T:379`).
- **Measured 15 s:** verdict `below_band`, which counts as a refutation, yet the gate passes and the plan holds.

The other cards' inputs show the same unfitness. Value 0 gives `no_band` (`localized_faults`, `acceptance_contract_ready`, `T:283,308`). Booleans and counts (`agreement_pass` unit "boolean", `admissible_caps` value 1) get a band [0.33, 3] that has no meaning for them.

**Smallest fix:** keep the band as the price-check column, as now. Add a row field `refutes`, defined as `gate_passed === false` when `gate_passed` is not null, and otherwise as the band verdict (`below_band`/`above_band`). Count `refuted_total` from `refutes`. Keep `verdict` unchanged, so nothing that reads it breaks.

### 2. `write_back_unfit`: the resolved state is taken from the band alone
`card_resolve.js` sets `refuted`/`calibrated` from band verdicts only, while each `resolved` entry already carries `gate_passed`. For the admissible record, a measured 100 s would mark the card `calibrated` although its own gate stops it. Later steps and the tree would read the opposite of the card's rule. This is the outcome s09 asked to avoid: "resolved by its own rule rather than by a ratio band" (`s09/ASSESSMENT.md:20`).

**Smallest fix:** add `refutes` (from fix 1) to each `resolved` entry. The state becomes `refuted` when the latest entry for any required id has `refutes: true`. It becomes `calibrated` when the latest entry for every required id has a measured value and `refutes: false`, meaning the gate passed, or the value was within the band when there is no gate. Otherwise the state stays unchanged.

### 3. `leaks_or_biases`: the harness can read the card's value and gate threshold
U54 places the full record in `A/card.json` "so an agent restricted to the run's folders can read it". The harness and anchors-repair agents can therefore see `value` 60 and the gate threshold 60. The rule "never the card's own `value`" is only an instruction. A harness that knows the target can steer toward it: it can choose a scale or a timeout around 60 s, or stop a slow case. That is the bias a calibration must exclude.

**Smallest fix:** the pipeline writes two copies.
- `A/card.json` for the agents, holding the record with `value`, `phase.gate.value`, `predictions` and `anchor.published_value` removed. Intake still gets the `published_value` it needs for anchors through its own prompt.
- The full copy, for `score_card.py` and `card_resolve.js` only, in a pipeline-only location outside the agents' readable folders (e.g. under `C/`), with the same `source_sha256`.

The prompts then name only the blinded copy.

### 4. Missing field `predictions` (decision_rule)
**Smallest fix:** in `main.js:478`, add `decision_rule: plan.predictions.decision_rule` to the record's `predictions`, and say so in the same CONTRACT.md change that adds `name`/`unit`. # s11 assessment: fixes chosen for the G2 contract (U54), 2026-11-03

**Scope.** No test, no network, no box contact, no git, no credentials. I read `science/s09/ASSESSMENT.md`, `science/s10/ASSESSMENT.md`, `science/s10/CHECK.json`, and the measure compiler `dut/pipeline/launch.js:55-108` for the band rule. Bash was denied in this session, so I hashed nothing. I wrote only into `science/s11/`. The choices are in `FIXES.json`. This file gives the reasons.

s10's finding (`s10/CHECK.json:1`): verdict `partial`, missing `predictions`, problems `band_rule_unfit`, `write_back_unfit`, `leaks_or_biases`.

## 1. `predictions`: `other`, `seal_record_before_box`, `return_in_scored`, `hide_from_agents`
- **`other` (needed, and no listed fix covers it).** The record never contains the plan's `decision_rule`. `main.js:478` builds `predictions` from only `if_lever, if_not, noise_rule, expected` (`s10/ASSESSMENT.md:18`). U54 copies the record unchanged, so every listed fix (sealing it, returning it, hiding it) acts on a record that has already lost the rule. **What `other` needs:** in `dut/pipeline/src/main.js` near line 478 (calibration record construction), add `decision_rule: plan.predictions.decision_rule` to the record's `predictions`. Document it in `dut/pipeline/CONTRACT.md` section 5 "calibration", in the same change that adds `name`/`unit`. This changes the tree's card records (`needs_tree_change: yes`).
- **`seal_record_before_box`.** U54 pins the record with `source_sha256`, but the owner's rule is "seal predictions before each test". The seal has to exist before any box command, and the score has to name it. Otherwise nothing shows the record that was scored is the record that was sealed.
- **`return_in_scored`.** G1 consumes the decision rule later (`s10/ASSESSMENT.md:51`; `s09/ASSESSMENT.md:36-38`). The scored file and the resolved copy must therefore carry `predictions` unchanged. A later step can then show that the final run used the card's own rule (`s09/ASSESSMENT.md:28`).
- **`hide_from_agents`.** This matches s10 fix 3: the agents' copy has `predictions` removed (`s10/ASSESSMENT.md:45`).
- **Not chosen: `judge_decision_rule`.** The admissible record's decision rule is about the full experiment ("Acceleration passes only after agreement and when 95% paired-median CPU/GPU complete-wall ratio…", `s10/ASSESSMENT.md:18`). A calibration that measures `eval_runtime_s` cannot evaluate it. G1 does that.

## 2. `band_rule_unfit`: `gate_decides`, `absolute_band_field`, `sign_aware`
- **`gate_decides`.** This is the core of s10 fix 1. For `eval_runtime_s` the band is [20, 180] s and the gate is ≤ 60 s. A measured 100 s would be `within_band` even though the gate stops the card. A measured 15 s would be `below_band` (refuted) even though the gate passes (`s10/ASSESSMENT.md:27-30`). The gate has to decide, and the band becomes a price-check column only.
- **`absolute_band_field`.** Some inputs have no gate, or their gate is on a different input. For those the band still decides. A value of 0 gets no band (`localized_faults`, `acceptance_contract_ready`), and booleans and small counts (`agreement_pass`, `admissible_caps` = 1) get a meaningless [0.33, 3] (`s10/ASSESSMENT.md:32`). Only a per-input absolute band supplied by the card makes these well defined, for example an exact match for a boolean. This is a new field in the card's records (tree change).
- **`sign_aware`.** In `launch.js:71-73` the band is `[value/k, value*k]`. For a negative value that band is inverted (lo > hi), so every measurement is out of band. No current required input is negative, but the seed's quality comparisons (P5/P6: dense − standard DockQ) are signed. The operator revises once, so I include this latent defect in the same rule.
- **Not chosen: `bounded_range`.** No current input is a fraction or probability. Booleans are better served by an absolute band. **Not chosen: `noise_band`.** Once the gate decides, replicates are not needed for this one-input record. They are needed for P2's tolerances, which is G3, not G2.

## 3. `write_back_unfit`: `as_plan_numbers`, `rejudge_card`, `all_runs_not_latest`, `record_run_identity`
- **`as_plan_numbers` and `rejudge_card`.** The owner asked to "carry promising candidates through calibration". Marking a state does not do that. The measured value must replace the GUESS as a MEASURED plan number with provenance, and the card's plan and cost (USD 9.87 line, `s10/ASSESSMENT.md:21`) must be re-judged with it. Otherwise the tree keeps pricing the card on the guess.
- **`all_runs_not_latest`.** s10's proposed rule uses "the latest entry for any required id" (`s10/ASSESSMENT.md:39`). With latest-wins, a refuting run can be erased by re-running until a pass, which breaks "preserve negative results". Any refuting run must keep the card refuted.
- **`record_run_identity`.** Once the state comes from all runs, the entries have to be comparable. P3 timing depends on box type (`s09/ASSESSMENT.md:43`), so each entry needs box type, pipeline commit and date.
- **Not chosen: `states_unfit`.** With `gate_decides`, `refuted` means "the card's own gate failed", and a re-judged card carries the rest. The two states then serve later steps.

## 4. `leaks_or_biases`: `hide_value`, `hide_predictions`, `hide_anchor_value`, `extraction_rule_before_run`
- **`hide_value`, `hide_predictions`, `hide_anchor_value`.** This is s10 fix 3: the agents' `A/card.json` has `value`, `phase.gate.value`, `predictions` and `anchor.published_value` removed, and the full copy is pipeline-only (`s10/ASSESSMENT.md:42-47`). A harness that knows the target of 60 s can choose scale or timeouts to hit it. The same holds for an anchor's published value.
- **`extraction_rule_before_run`.** U54 keeps the card value out of the measured key "at least by instruction" (`s10/ASSESSMENT.md:7`). Even when the harness is blind, if it chooses which output line becomes `card:<id>`, it still chooses the measurement. Fixing the read rule before the run and having the pipeline apply it closes that gap.

## Summary
One item includes `other`: the decision rule must be added to the tree's calibration record (`main.js:478`). Two fixes need tree record changes: that one, and the per-input absolute band field. No narrowing. No test, no predictions. Next action: stop, `contract_gap`, pending the operator's single revision of U54.
# s12 assessment: content check of the revised G2 contract (U54, U55, U56), 2026-11-03

**Scope.** No test, no network, no box contact, no git, no credentials. Bash was denied in this session, so I hashed nothing and did not open the `metis-wt` worktree. I judged U54, U55 and U56 as quoted verbatim in the step brief. I read `science/s09/` (ASSESSMENT.md, REQS.json), `s10/` (ASSESSMENT.md, CHECK.json), `s11/` (ASSESSMENT.md, FIXES.json, NARROWING.md), the tree result `experiments/blind-02/20261103-0124-tree/out/result.json` (T below) at lines 253–412, `dut/pipeline/src/main.js:309–316, 434, 465–480`, `src/cost.js:154, 222–334`, `src/gates.js:201–254`, and the producer plan `T/../out/work/seed-20261103/seed/idea/370cabd5/producer.md:68, 97–100, 563–569`. I judge G2 only, not G1, G3 or G6. I wrote only into `science/s12/`.

## Verdict: sufficient (build as written)

Every REQS.json G2 field is carried, and every fix s11 chose in `s11/FIXES.json` is met, including the `other` (the decision rule), which the revision delivers by a different route from the one s11 proposed. I found no remaining problem from the code list. Under "Build notes" I list four points for the build. None of them blocks G2.

## Fields (s09/REQS.json G2: `name, unit, basis, value, differs_in, measured_by, phase, anchor, predictions, measured_value`, direction both)

| Field | Carried | Where |
|---|---|---|
| name, unit | yes | U55 copies them from the plan's `numbers` into each `required` item. U54 passes them to agents in `A/card_inputs.json` and to the score rows. For the admissible input they are "Maximum complete per-case evaluation runtime; unknown until agreement", "seconds" (`producer.md:564–565`). |
| basis, value, differs_in, measured_by, phase | yes | They are in the record (`main.js:473–474`), which is sealed unchanged in `C/card.json`. `basis` and `value` are copied into the rows, and `phase.gate` decides. |
| anchor | yes | The record's anchor is sealed. Only `anchor.what` reaches agents. The scored `anchor` block reports published, tolerance, measured, difference and passed, and the anchor never decides an input. For the admissible record `published_value` is a string (`T:393`), so the anchor is correctly null. |
| predictions | yes | The record's four keys are sealed and returned unchanged in `card_scored.json`. The decision rule is carried through U55's `judged.plan` (see the `other` fix below). |
| measured_value | yes | It is read by the sealed extraction rule into `rows[].measured_value`, then written to `resolved[].measured_value` and to the MEASURED `number`. |

`missing`: none.

## s11's fixes, one by one

### predictions
- **`other` (decision rule into the record): met.** s11 asked for `decision_rule` to be added to the record's `predictions` (`s11/ASSESSMENT.md`, §1). U55 does not do that. Instead it adds `judged.plan`, "the plan the record's `plan_usd` was evaluated from". That is the plan `main.js:434` evaluates, and its `predictions.decision_rule` is mandatory: `gate_plan` halts a plan whose decision rule has no number (`gates.js:211`). The plan therefore reaches every place s11 needed it:
  - it is sealed in `C/card.json` as part of the record unchanged, before any box command;
  - it is bound to the score by `card_scored.card_sha256`;
  - it is carried in `card_resolve.js`'s copy of the calibration array.

  G1 can therefore show that a final run used the card's own rule. A reader must take it from `judged.plan.predictions.decision_rule`, not from the record's `predictions`. This should be documented, but it is not a defect.
- **`seal_record_before_box`: met.** `C/card.json` and `C/card_seal.json` are written atomically before the intake call and before any box command. Every later read uses `C/card.json`. `score_card.py` and `card_resolve.js` both check the seal.
- **`return_in_scored`: met.** `card_scored.json` carries `predictions` unchanged and `card_sha256`.
- **`hide_from_agents`: met.** `A/card_inputs.json` explicitly excludes predictions.

### band_rule_unfit
- **`gate_decides`: met.** `gate_passed` is computed when `phase.gate.on` equals the item id, and the gate then decides (`decided_by: "gate"`). For `eval_runtime_s` (gate `<= 60`, `T:375–380`), a measured 100 s now refutes and a measured 15 s now holds. Those were the two contradictions s10 found (`s10/ASSESSMENT.md` §1).
- **`absolute_band_field`: met.** There are two sources. One is the plan's optional `band {abs: x}` (U55). The other is launch `bands`, which are sealed in `C/card.json` before the run. With them, zero values (`localized_faults`, `acceptance_contract_ready`, `T:283, 308`) and booleans become judgeable.
- **`sign_aware`: met.** A negative value gets `[value*k, value/k]`.

### write_back_unfit
- **`as_plan_numbers`: met.** Each measured entry carries a MEASURED number with the fields the plan schema requires for MEASURED (`command`, `output`, `output_line`, `machine`; `schemas.js:233–236`).
- **`rejudge_card`: met.** The replaced plan is re-run through the tree's own `cost_eval_plan(plan, given)` and `gate_plan(plan, ev, pick, args)`, with the `given` and `args` recorded at judging. That matches the tree's calls (`main.js:309, 434`), which pass no third `opts` argument. A MEASURED number with `differs_in: []` is no longer uncertain (`cost.js:154`), so `uncertain_after` drops it.
- **`all_runs_not_latest`: met.** Any `refuted` entry from any named run makes the card `refuted`. The re-judged value is the median over all runs.
- **`record_run_identity`: met.** Each entry records `run`, `pipeline_commit`, `box_type` and `box_started_utc`.

### leaks_or_biases
- **`hide_value`, `hide_predictions`, `hide_anchor_value`: met.** Agents see only `{id, name, unit, measured_by, phase.what}` and `anchor.what`. Card mode never names `C/` or `result`. For the admissible record none of those strings contains the value or the threshold of 60: `phase.what` is at `T:374` and the name at `producer.md:564`. The 60 appears only in `gate.value` and `gate.else` (`T:378–379`) and in the number's `rests_on`, and none of these reaches agents.
- **`extraction_rule_before_run`: met.** `card_extract.json` is declared by the harness agent and validated by the pipeline. It is sealed before the harness upload, never changed by a repair, and applied by `score_card.py`, not by a harness script.

`problems`: none.

## Build notes (not blocking; no code applies)
1. **Aggregated inputs.** `eval_runtime_s` is a maximum over cases (`producer.md:564`). The rule kinds (a JSON Pointer, or the last regex match) cannot take a maximum, so the harness must write the aggregate itself. The harness prompt says "no harness script computes, writes or asserts a card value." The build should word this so that writing a measured aggregate is clearly allowed and only targeting or copying a card value is forbidden. The alternative is an optional `agg` (`max|min|median|mean|sum`) on a rule over an array or all matches. Bias is not at stake here, because the harness is blind to the value.
2. **Card bands will be absent in practice.** U55 changes no prompt, so the producer never emits `band`. For non-positive or boolean inputs the operative route is launch `bands`. The science step that writes the m5 brief must set them, and they are sealed in `C/card.json`.
3. **Free-text leakage.** `phase.what` and `name` are plan prose. A future card could state a threshold in them, and the pipeline cannot strip numbers from prose. This does not happen for the admissible record. The brief given to the run must likewise contain no card values (that is the science step's responsibility).
4. **Run omission.** `card_resolve.js` judges only the run roots it is given. A later call that leaves out a refuting run would read `calibrated`. Earlier output files are never overwritten, so the negative result persists on disk. Science steps must pass every run that measured the card.

The admissible record today is `seed:idea:2` (`T:358–404`; one GUESS input, line USD 9.87). To give it `judged`, the tree must first be rerun with `--resume` on T's out dir. U55 states that this reproduces T's states and adds only the new fields.

## Predictions and outcomes
s11 sealed no predictions, so `outcomes.json` is empty. This step runs no test, so `predictions.json` is empty. Next action: stop, `contract_gap`. The revision is sufficient for G2, and building it is the operator's next step. G1, G3 and G6 remain open and were not judged here.

### A/method/ and remote execution interface
- The method author writes three required nonempty files: `method.patch` (git-style paths relative to the published source root), `setup_method.sh`, and `run_method.sh`. An optional fourth file, `run_anchors.sh`, implements the method anchor protocol. No other files are allowed. Shell scripts must pass `bash -n`. The pipeline copies them from the private view into `A/method/`; neither author writes control state.
- Each attempt uploads method files to remote `payload/method/` and frozen tests/fixtures to `payload/tests/`. Uploads append independently decodable base64 chunks of at most 24,576 characters, batching commands below 32,768 characters to avoid shell argument limits; each batch has its own receipt. It creates a fresh source copy at `method/` using `cp -a baseline-published method`; patch checking and application use `git apply` with an explicit detached Git context and that copy as work tree, so copied repository/worktree metadata cannot redirect writes into the baseline. A retry always starts from a fresh copy.
- The scripts run from the same remote run directory used by reproduce: `bash payload/method/setup_method.sh`, then `bash payload/method/run_method.sh`, then `bash payload/tests/run_tests.sh`. All receive absolute environment paths `BASELINE_DIR` (original published source), `METHOD_DIR` (patched source copy), `BASELINE_OUT` (frozen baseline outputs), and `METHOD_OUT` (remote `out/`). Setup builds the patched copy; run uses the same representative scale, inputs and seeds and writes actual method outputs in exactly the baseline's format and relative output locations. The method author prompt and the method repair prompt list the frozen `method_outputs` paths and state that `run_method.sh` writes each of them under `METHOD_OUT` at that relative path, as the baseline outputs do. After `run_method.sh` exits 0 and its `out/` is fetched, and before any test command, implement checks that every `method_outputs` path exists in that fetched copy as a file or symlink. When any is missing the attempt fails with pipeline failure category `layout` and the tests are not run for that attempt. Fixtures resolve relative to `run_tests.sh`. Remote `out/` is cleared before setup and again before method execution; `out/tests.json` is removed immediately before tests. A previous baseline/method/report cannot satisfy a new attempt.
- `A/implement-payload.json` records the current attempt with exactly `{attempt, remote_directory, baseline_directory, method_directory, baseline_outputs, method_outputs, tests_sha256, seal_sha256, method_files, timeouts}`. `attempt` is 1 or 2. Relative directory values are `baseline-published`, `method`, `baseline-out`, and `out`; `remote_directory` is the absolute shared remote directory. `method_files` contains `{path, sha256}` for every provided method file, using relative names and SHA-256 of exact bytes. `timeouts` has positive integer seconds for `setup_method`, `run_method`, `run_tests`. Hashes are lowercase 64-digit hexadecimal strings. The payload is regenerated after repair and reviewed only in its final form.

### A/tests/ and out/tests.json
- wf exposes `agent.journal`, the absolute journal path. Cached journal events now include `model`, preserved from the successful result in the resume source. Cached answers retain model provenance but incur no new token usage. Failed attempts and unused shadow answers do not replace the answering family.
- New `C/stages/<stage>.json` receipts contain `{stage, status, wall_s, gpu_s, usd, model_family, notes}`, plus any stage-provided v1 overrides and measured token counts. Stage/status/model families use their existing enums. `notes` is an array with either no entries or the single fixed code `multiple_model_families`; no model text, prompts, filenames, or scientific facts are copied into it. These receipts are separate from `C/receipts/` box command receipts.
- Both serve and dev `lambda_serve.sh up` write `$HOME/.cache/metis-serve/box.json` atomically alongside `state.json`. Its keys are `{type, region, price_usd_h, started_utc}`: Lambda instance-type and region identifiers, a numeric hourly USD price, and a UTC ISO timestamp. Repeated state saves preserve the allocation's start. Confirmed `down` retains `box.json` and adds `ended_utc` (UTC ISO timestamp) and `hours` (nonnegative elapsed allocation hours, including startup and termination polling). State archival behavior is unchanged. The next `up` replaces this record for the new allocation.
- At the start of reproduce, the pipeline copies the current shared `box.json` to `C/box.json`, replacing any stale run copy. Missing box metadata leaves pricing unavailable and stage USD at zero. At takeaways, a matching allocation record can refresh the copy with its confirmed end; a different allocation never replaces the snapshot. If reproduce was skipped, takeaways snapshots the current allocation to account for any run overlap.
- Box receipts add numeric nonnegative `gpu_busy_s` and boolean `gpu_busy_known`. The detached remote script writes `<receipt-id>.gpu` beside its log, sampling `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=utilization.gpu --format=csv,noheader,nounits` immediately and every 2 seconds until the command exits or times out. Each finite utilization sample in [0,100] contributes `utilization / 100 * 2` seconds; samples from every GPU are summed. Missing/invalid samples contribute nothing. No valid samples means `gpu_busy_s=0`, `gpu_busy_known=false`. Telemetry collection failure does not change command/fetch success. Sampling survives loss of the local polling process; the remote runner stops sampling before publishing its exit marker.
- Stage v1 `gpu_s` sums its box receipts' `gpu_busy_s`, including failed commands and retries. **Full comparison:** GPU-standard3600 versus GPU-dense54000 rotations, CPU-standard affordability reference, fixed four cases and50 poses. Separate signed per-case changes in rank1 and best50 DockQ.
